\section{Related Work}\label{sec:related}

\paragraph{Test-time compute scaling.}
Self-consistency \cite{wang2023selfconsistency} and best-of-$N$ \cite{snell2025scaling, brown2024monkeys} drive large gains on reasoning and code.
Reward-free selectors \cite{taubenfeld2025cisc, kang2025selfcertainty}, BoN scaling laws \cite{gao2023scaling}, adaptive allocation \cite{aggarwal2023adaptive}, and trained verifiers \cite{cobbe2021verifiers, lightman2024verify} all target discrete-answer settings; structured prediction requires different aggregation because degeneracy operates at the entity-set level.

\paragraph{SC failure modes and fine-grained variants.}
\citet{chen2023twofailures} identify SC failures in reasoning (hypothetical, compositional) where consistent outputs are systematically wrong; our correlation-selection gap is a distinct structured-generation failure where signals \textit{correlate} with quality yet fail to \textit{select}.
\citet{chen2024usc} extend SC to free-form tasks via universal matching; our diagnostic framework shows such extensions face limits under constrained decoding (\S\ref{sec:selection_gap}).
\citet{thirukovalluru2024atomic} decompose long-form claims into atomic units for consistency scoring; our entity-level decomposition shares this sub-structure intuition but reveals that sub-output agreement does not translate to selection gain.

\paragraph{Consistency for structured IE.}
\citet{yao2026consistency} show consistency correlates with NER/RE accuracy; we diagnose degeneracy and LP compression as mechanisms that prevent this correlation from yielding selection gains.
\citet{xie2023zeroshot} propose entity voting for zero-shot NER; our approach aggregates stochastic samples from a fine-tuned model.
We build on generative IE \cite{zhou2024uniner, sainz2024gollie} and constrained decoding \cite{willard2023guided, dong2024xgrammar}.

\paragraph{Uncertainty estimation and MBR.}
Our selection instantiates MBR decoding \cite{eikema2022sampling}; \citet{eikema2025structured} find MBR utilities degrade on structured outputs.
Semantic entropy \cite{kuhn2023semantic, farquhar2024detecting} clusters generations by meaning, but equivalence classes are ill-defined for entity sets with partial overlap.
Calibrated structured prediction \cite{kuleshov2015calibrated} grounds confidence in structured outputs; LP compression (\S\ref{sec:selection_gap}) identifies a practical failure mode under constrained decoding.
Confidence estimation \cite{geng2024confidence, xia2025survey} and selective prediction \cite{geifman2017selective} provide complementary alternatives.

\subsection{Capability Ceiling vs.\ Diversity Collapse}\label{sec:yun_contrast}

\citet{yun2025price} identify \textit{diversity collapse}: constrained decoding suppresses token-level diversity.
Our LP compression (median range 0.041 nats) corroborates this but diverges in root cause, diagnostic depth, and evidence scope.

Diversity collapse attributes failure to format-imposed constraints; our capability ceiling diagnosis implicates model-internal factors---entity-level degeneracy (17.8--67.9\%), self-verification failure (ESJ AUROC $0.51$), and a complexity-dependent introspection boundary (probe AUROC $0.63$\textendash$0.88$)---that persist independently of decoding format.
Our four-stage cascade (\S\ref{sec:selection_gap}) decomposes failure into independently testable stages, localizing the bottleneck to within-instance LP alignment rather than diversity per se; seven entity-level self-verification methods systematically fail (\S\ref{sec:mechanistic}, \S\ref{sec:adaptive}), providing mechanistic evidence absent from diversity collapse analysis.
We additionally test persistence at $4{\times}$ scale (Qwen2.5-72B, $+1.2$\,pp; \S\ref{sec:scaling}).

\subsection{Cross-Model Self-Consistency}\label{sec:cross_model}

Diversity from stochastic sampling within a single model is limited by architecture-specific degeneracy (\S\ref{sec:selection_gap}).
Mixing samples from architecturally distinct models---which produce complementary error patterns---can partially bypass this bottleneck.

2	
3	Since instance-level selection fails (\S\ref{sec:selection_gap}), we present approaches that extract value from multi-sample generation beyond single-signal sample ranking.

5	\subsection{Cross-Model Self-Consistency}\label{sec:cross_model}
6	
7	Mixing samples from architecturally distinct models can partially bypass within-model degeneracy.
8	Combining 4 samples each from Qwen3-8B and LLaMA-3.1-8B (Few-NERD) yields $+0.42$\,pp over pure LLaMA ($p{<}0.001$, CI $[0.27, 0.58]$; $N{=}8$ total).
9	
10	\subsection{Trained Verifiers: High Discrimination, Low Transfer}\label{sec:verifier}
11	
12	A LightGBM entity-level classifier (5 features: agreement count, LP, VC, SJ, FK) achieves AUC${=}0.923{\pm}0.002$ under out-of-fold evaluation, confirming that entity correctness is learnable from the available signals.
13	Yet this discrimination translates poorly to F1: OOF construction yields only $+0.30$\,pp overall, with per-dataset gains of $+1.28$\,pp on SciERC, $+0.55$\,pp on CoNLL, and $+0.02$\,pp on Few-NERD.
14	The near-zero Few-NERD gain despite AUC${>}0.92$ reveals that frequency-based threshold construction (\S\ref{sec:prescriptive}) already captures most of the verifier's signal; SciERC---with low degeneracy and diverse entity-level errors---is the exception where learned discrimination adds value beyond majority vote.
15	Cross-dataset transfer remains negative (B2-v2: $-0.76$\,pp; B2-v3: $-1.02$\,pp on Few-NERD; Appendix~\ref{app:verifier_transfer}), confirming dataset-specific feature mappings.
16	Even a trained discriminator with near-perfect entity classification cannot close the aggregation gap, indicating the bottleneck is structural rather than a matter of signal quality.
